caption: Choices that are easy to defend, each with its condition

columns.label: Why it is easy to defend

rows.choice: Native HTML, such as dialog and popover. Components without styles, such as Base UI or Radix Primitives.
rows.why: The keyboard and the roles are built in. State is an attribute, and no style is written at run time.
rows.condition: The styles are static CSS, and no data is written into the page as HTML.

rows.choice: Static CSS in layers. Tokens in the Design Tokens format. A utility framework whose output is a static file.
rows.why: No script is needed, so the strict policy for styles holds.
rows.condition: No style attribute, and no CSS that is put together from text at run time.

rows.choice: Open icon sets as SVG in the page. Open typefaces as files on your own server.
rows.why: No request leaves your server, and the licences are open.
rows.condition: Each file is listed with its checksum and its licence.

rows.choice: A secrets manager, with short-lived identities for the pipeline.
rows.why: Each read is logged, and a key can be changed in one place.
rows.condition: A scan for secrets runs on every change.

rows.choice: A lock file, an install without scripts, and a bill of materials in the CycloneDX format.
rows.why: A reviewer can compare what runs with what was approved.
rows.condition: The pipeline fails on a known serious weakness, and on a step that is not pinned.

rows.choice: An open standard, such as OpenTelemetry, with a filter before anything leaves.
rows.why: The data has one known shape, and it is not tied to one company.
rows.condition: The filter allows only named fields, and removes personal data.
